terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the till here and print values to look inside them.

tasks.title: Add up the order total
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/till.js`, `totalCents` should be the price of the candles plus shipping, in cents, as a number. It comes out wrong, with no error. Find the line that makes the wrong value and fix it. `shippingText` arrives as text from the courier's price list, and that line stays as it is.

Check runs the lines of Task 1 alone, with other amounts in `candlesCents` and `shippingText`, and reads `totalCents`: it must be a number, the two amounts added.
nextSteps: Run `node src/till.js` and compare the total with the example in the comment.
Print `typeof totalCents` to see what kind of value it is.
Print each of the two amounts and its type, and find the one that is not a number.
Fix the line that makes `totalCents`, and run the file again.
hints: The total looks like the two amounts written side by side. Which operator does that to text?
`+` with text on either side joins instead of adding. `shippingText` holds digits, but it is text.
Turn the shipping into a number inside the sum: `candlesCents + Number(shippingText)`.

tasks.title: Count the candles packed
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, `candlesPacked` should start at zero and have the boxes Ines packed added to it, each box holding `candlesPerBox` candles. It comes out as `NaN`. Find out why and fix it.

Check runs the lines of Task 2 alone, with other numbers in `boxesPacked` and `candlesPerBox`, and reads `candlesPacked`: it must be a number, every candle in every box.
nextSteps: Run the file and read what the count prints.
Add a line that prints `candlesPacked` right before the line that adds to it.
Ask what a sum gives when one of its parts holds that.
Fix it so the count starts where the comment says, and run the file again.
hints: NaN came out of a sum. Print each part of that sum, on the line before it.
A `let` made without a value holds `undefined`, and `undefined` plus a number is `NaN`.
Give the count its starting value where it is made: `let candlesPacked = 0`.

tasks.title: Measure the label
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, `labelLength` should be how many characters `labelLine` has. It comes out as `undefined`, with no error. Find the mistake and fix it.

Check runs the lines of Task 3 alone, with another label in `labelLine`, and reads `labelLength`: it must be a number, the length of that label.
nextSteps: Run the file and read what the label length prints.
Print `typeof labelLength`, then print `labelLine` itself: is the label there?
If the label is there, look closely at what the line asks the label for.
Fix it and run the file again.
hints: The label is fine, so the problem is in what the line asks it for.
Asking text for something it does not have gives `undefined` instead of an error. Spelling counts, as it does for names.
The word after the dot is misspelt: it is `labelLine.length`.
